note: Dimensions are reused from the F0-03 prosperity measurement framework V0.1 draft. No weighted or aggregate prosperity score is defined or permitted.

dimensions.title: Economic security
dimensions.summary: Real household resources relative to local prices, volatility of income or consumption, difficulty meeting essential expenses and capacity to absorb shocks.
dimensions.measurementPitfall: Income is not the same as disposable resources; transfers, informal earnings, household size and inflation all matter.

dimensions.title: Essential needs
dimensions.summary: Verified receipt of eligible support, housing and energy cost burden, safe services and food security.
dimensions.measurementPitfall: Programme take-up does not necessarily translate into reduced hardship; self-reported and administrative measures have different errors.

dimensions.title: Health and learning
dimensions.summary: Affordable access to and continuity of care, attendance and educational progression.
dimensions.measurementPitfall: Sensitive data need strong consent, safeguarding and minimisation; utilisation can rise when illness worsens.

dimensions.title: Opportunity
dimensions.summary: Sustained net earnings, job quality and stability, and equitable access to practical choices.
dimensions.measurementPitfall: Training attendance is not employment; jobs may displace opportunities for others; selection bias and local labour demand matter.

dimensions.title: Autonomy, fairness and sustainability
dimensions.summary: Time spent navigating services, meaningful choice, unequal treatment, and burdens shifted onto others or future generations.
dimensions.measurementPitfall: Question wording and cultural interpretation vary; subjective measures require a validated local instrument.

problemFamilies.title: Access to existing benefits and services
problemFamilies.summary: People entitled to assistance may not receive it because of awareness, administrative requirements, stigma, digital exclusion or complex processes.
problemFamilies.pillarRole: First worked cross-context example (Solutions & Experimentation Engine).

problemFamilies.title: Affordability of essential needs
problemFamilies.summary: Household energy and housing costs can erode living standards; the burden varies strongly by housing stock, climate, pricing and support systems.
problemFamilies.pillarRole: Second problem family, beginning with household energy; housing is a registered research question with an explicit evidence gap.

problemFamilies.title: Economic opportunity, employment quality and livelihoods
problemFamilies.summary: Insufficient access to quality jobs and reliable earnings prevents many households from escaping poverty.
problemFamilies.pillarRole: Third problem family with evidence-linked templates; no validated HPI intervention.

problemFamilies.title: Economic systems, distribution and household security
problemFamilies.summary: Why aggregate growth and productivity do not always translate into proportionate improvements in household security.
problemFamilies.pillarRole: Economic Systems Lab research agenda (long-term horizon B, starting with bounded questions now).
